findings: Exact x86_64 manifest, iOS18.5 runtime, iPhone16 type, available boolean and Shutdown state required for existing selection.
Malformed inventory, invalid or duplicated UUID, or enumeration timeout fails; none silently falls back to creation. Multiple exact eligible devices use deterministic UUID order.
Selection happens after immutable host/Xcode/SDK/app Mach-O/signature verification. Actual runtime/version and selected device identity/state are rechecked before boot.
Both boot and bootstatus -b must succeed for the same verified UUID before app digest recheck and install. Existing setup budgets remain unchanged.
Provenance distinguishes existing-shutdown versus fresh-creation and explicitly records createdByThisInvocation. Preboot proof no longer claims a reused device was freshly created.
Cleanup targets only the selected UUID; shutdown is allowed for either path, delete only for a device created by this invocation. No global reset, cache purge or service termination.
Original iOS sign-in retains clearState:true and clearKeychain:true; unchanged diagnostic flow requires actual reader, page titles and next-page assertions.
No rebuild, rebundle, resign, application source edits, UI deadline change or acceptance weakening.
limits: Controlled actual Python selector/setup/cleanup execution, not a new macOS Simulator result.
The next host may still have CoreSimulator metadata or boot delays; this change avoids unnecessary create only when an exact verified preexisting device is available.
Native app/UI readiness still requires the unchanged diagnostic to pass.
The tested app remains original d46, not the newly restored local reader deadline code.
